name: Iris Nakamura
equipment: A Speed Graphic press camera with a flash gun, twelve film holders and a box of flashbulbs (24)
A Leica, small, for when the Speed Graphic is too obvious
.32 pocket pistol (Colt 1908), 8 rounds loaded, which her father bought her in 1946 and made her promise to carry
A Ledger press card and a PRESS card in her hatband
A canvas camera bag with a darkroom kit: a changing bag, developer, fixer and a red safelight bulb
Her negatives: a card-file box of every negative she has shot since 1940, indexed, including the 1947 Kessling execution vigil
A green eyeshade, a fountain pen, and the Ledger photo desk's petty-cash book, which she keeps because nobody else can add
A raincoat, a man's fedora and flat shoes for running
features: Knows the Block (City-Born origin: in Port Calloway she knows every back way, alley, bar and payphone and who they belong to; advantage on Streetwise checks to find a person, place or service in the city)

Press Pass (Reporter: with her press card in her hatband she gets into crime scenes, press boxes, courtrooms and the coroner's office; a source who talks to her is never burned by her, and her sources know it)
The Morgue (Reporter: her Research checks take half the usual time, and once per long rest she can find one fact the Ledger has printed, or photographed, about a named person, business or address)

Ink by the Barrel (Reporter, 2nd level: when she threatens to print, or publish a photograph of, what she knows about someone with a reputation to protect, she can use INT for the Intimidation check and has advantage on it)

Beat: Photographer (Reporter, 3rd level: as an action, fire a flashbulb at a creature within 15 ft: CON save, DC 12, or blinded until the end of its next turn; her photographs are evidence that police, editors and juries accept)
Ability Score Improvement (Reporter, 4th level: +1 Intelligence, +1 Charisma)
Follow the Money (Bookkeeper background: give her a ledger, a bank statement or a set of books for an hour and she will find what does not add up)

personality.traits: I watch. I say very little and I notice everything, and then I take one picture, and it is the one that runs. I am funny, drily, once people know me, and almost nobody knows me.
personality.ideals: A photograph is a witness that cannot be bribed, frightened or deported. I take pictures so that what happened cannot be made not to have happened.
personality.bonds: My parents, who ran Nakamura Grocery on Jackson Street for twenty years, lost it in 1942 when we were sent to the camp in Idaho, and have built it again from nothing since 1945. And the Ledger, which kept my job open for three years and printed a front-page editorial against the evacuation in 1942 when no other paper on the coast would.
personality.flaws: I do not forgive. I remember every face in every crowd that watched us get on the buses in 1942, and some of them are on Larch Hill now, and one of them owns the Courier. I would like very much to take his picture on the worst day of his life.

appearance: A slight, straight-backed woman of thirty-one with a pale oval face, short black hair under a man's fedora, black-rimmed glasses, and a camera always somewhere on her. She wears a belted raincoat and flat shoes. She moves quietly and stands very still, and people forget she is there, which is how she likes it.
backstory: Iris Nakamura was born above her parents' grocery on Jackson Street and was the first Nisei hired by any newspaper in Port Calloway, as a darkroom girl at the Ledger in 1939, then a photographer in 1941. In May 1942 she and her family were sent with every other Japanese-American family in the city to an assembly center and then to a camp in the Idaho desert, where she kept the books for the camp's cooperative store and took photographs with a camera that was officially forbidden. Hollis Gage wrote to her every month. In 1945 she came back to the Ledger and her job. She photographed the Halvorsen ruin the morning after the fire, the Kessling trial and the execution vigil in the rain, and she has never thought the story was finished. On Tuesday, when private detectives come into the Ledger morgue asking for the Halvorsen envelope, she follows them out.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Iris is the party's camera and the Ledger's conscience. Use her to make evidence real: a photograph of Dunleavy at the Pelican back stair, of Teague's face, of the gun swap in the balcony, of the Courier's HOLD page. Her 1947 negative of the execution vigil shows young Nora Kessling standing beside Constance Muir, the future Mrs. Sloane, which is a clue to who sent the photostat. She is a companion from pa-scenario-001 (the Ledger) through pa-scenario-004, when Hollis Gage gives her press seats at the Regent. She will go anywhere for a picture and nowhere for a fight.
dmNotes.voice: Quiet, dry, exact. Short sentences. A deadpan wit that takes people a moment to notice. Calls Hollis Gage 'the old man' and Pip Ashdown 'Ashdown'. When she is angry she goes silent and takes a photograph.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: the picture that proves it. Secondary: the Ledger, and Hollis Gage. Tertiary: Cornelius Vantreight's face on the morning he is indicted, at f/8 and a hundredth of a second.
dmNotes.secrets: She knows something about Vantreight that is not in this case: in 1942 the Courier printed the addresses of Japanese-American businesses 'available for lease', and Calloway Holdings bought eleven of them, including her parents' first shop, for a tenth of their value. She has the Courier clippings and the deeds. It is not a crime. It is the reason she is in this story, and she will tell the party only if one of them asks her why she cares.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: reserved, then a fierce, quiet loyalty. Toward Pip Ashdown: rivalry and real affection; they argue about everything. Toward Nora Kessling: a big-sister protectiveness, since they work in the same building and Iris has watched her come in every day for two years. Toward Dunleavy: she has photographed him three times at places he should not have been, and he does not know. Toward Vantreight: see secrets.
